2026-11-26.meal: Creamy mushroom & butter bean stroganoff with rice
2026-11-26.note: Free evening, nothing on for tea — a new one to try to round off the week.

ingredients: 1 tbsp olive oil, plus a knob of butter
steps: Soften the onion in the oil and butter for 5 minutes. Add the mushrooms and cook for 5–6 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic and paprika and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the butter beans and stock and simmer for 8–10 minutes until slightly thickened.
Take out Mathilda's portion now, keeping hers plain.
Stir the crème fraîche through the rest and warm gently for 2–3 minutes — don't let it boil hard or it can split.
Cook the rice while the sauce finishes. Serve the stroganoff over rice, scattered with parsley.
recipe.tip: Mathilda: keep hers without the paprika, and mash a few of the butter beans if she's fussy about texture.

2026-11-27.meal: Veggie bean & sweet potato chilli (double batch)
2026-11-27.note: Gymnastics 9:30am & swimming 1:30pm today, evening's free — good day to batch-cook extra for Monday's parents' evening

ingredients: 2 sweet potatoes, peeled and cut into small cubes
Grated cheese & soured cream, to serve (optional)
steps: Soften the onions and peppers in the oil in a large pan for 8 minutes.
Add the garlic, cumin and paprika and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the sweet potato, beans, chopped tomatoes and tomato purée. Season, cover and simmer for 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick and the sweet potato is tender.
Take out Mathilda's portion, plus 4 portions to cool for Monday, before stirring the chilli flakes through the rest.
Cook the rice for 15 minutes before serving. Serve tonight's chilli over rice with cheese and soured cream if using.
Cool Monday's 4 portions within an hour, then cover and keep in the fridge (no need to freeze for just 3 days).
recipe.tip: Mathilda: take hers out before the chilli flakes go in. The sweet potato bulks it out so the Monday portions are properly filling.

2026-11-28.note: Sarah's engagement party 6-7pm — tea out tonight, no cooking. Alex back from CYCLONE and onto Christmas leave.

2026-11-29.meal: Slow-cooker beef & root veg stew with mash & greens
2026-11-29.note: This week's one meat night, and Alex's first Sunday home. Francis's hockey fixture today (time still TBC) — slow cooker on by 9am so tea's ready whenever you're back

ingredients: 1 Savoy cabbage or bag of greens
steps: Toss the beef in the flour. Brown it in the oil in a hot pan for 5 minutes (skip this if you're short on time — it still works).
Put the onions, carrots, swede, celery and garlic in the slow cooker and sit the beef on top.
Mix the tomato purée and Worcestershire into the stock, pour over, and add the bay and thyme.
Cover and cook on low for 7-8 hours until the beef falls apart.
Boil the potatoes for 15 minutes, drain and mash with a little butter and milk.
Shred the cabbage and boil or steam for 4-5 minutes.
Serve the stew over the mash with the greens alongside.
recipe.tip: Mathilda: shred her beef small and mash in a few carrots. Any leftovers freeze well (cooked and cooled first).

2026-11-30.meal: Reheat: Friday's bean & sweet potato chilli with rice
2026-11-30.note: Preschool Parents' Evening 6-7:30pm — quick reheat gets tea done before you head out

ingredients: 4 portions of Friday's chilli (from the fridge)
steps: Tip the chilli into a pan with a splash of water.
Heat gently, stirring, until bubbling and piping hot all the way through (about 8-10 minutes). Or microwave in a covered bowl for 4-5 minutes, stirring halfway.
Cook the rice while the chilli heats.
Serve straightaway, with cheese or soured cream if there's any left.
recipe.tip: Only reheat it once, and check it's piping hot all the way through before you head out the door.

2026-12-01.meal: Air-fryer frozen fishcakes with mash & peas
2026-12-01.note: Hull hockey training 6-7pm (Hymers College) plus travel — air fryer gets tea done fast either side

ingredients: 10 frozen fishcakes (3 each for the grown-ups)
900g potatoes for mash, or 5 microwave pouches
Butter & milk, for the mash (if making fresh)
steps: Air fry the fishcakes at 190°C for 12-15 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and piping hot all the way through (check the pack for exact timing; do two batches if they don't fit).
If making fresh mash, boil chunked potatoes for 15 minutes, drain, then mash with butter and a splash of milk.
Cook the peas and sweetcorn in a pan of boiling water for 4-5 minutes, or microwave.
Drain and serve everything together.
recipe.tip: Mathilda: cut hers into pieces and check it's piping hot through the middle before serving.

2026-12-02.meal: Air-fryer halloumi & veg wraps with sweet potato wedges
2026-12-02.note: Hockey Academy Night 6:15-7:45pm (The Lindum) — a new one to try, ready in 20 minutes either side of the run

ingredients: 2 x 225g blocks halloumi, cut into thick strips
400g tin chickpeas, drained and patted dry
steps: Heat the air fryer to 200°C. Toss the sweet potato wedges in 1/2 tbsp oil and air fry for 18-20 minutes, shaking halfway. Keep warm.
Toss the peppers, courgette and chickpeas in 1/2 tbsp oil with the oregano and air fry for 8 minutes.
Add the halloumi strips brushed with the rest of the oil and cook for a further 6-8 minutes, turning halfway, until golden.
Meanwhile mix the yoghurt, cucumber, garlic and a squeeze of lemon for the tzatziki. Season.
Warm the flatbreads for the last minute.
Fill the wraps with salad, veg, chickpeas and halloumi, spoon over the tzatziki, and serve the wedges alongside.
recipe.tip: Mathilda: plain halloumi, veg and a few wedges with a little plain yoghurt, no garlic. Grown-ups get two wraps each.

2026-12-03.meal: Mediterranean baked cod with tomatoes, chickpeas & couscous
2026-12-03.note: Free evening — a new one to try to round off the week

ingredients: Handful pitted black olives (for the grown-ups)
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Put the cherry tomatoes and chickpeas in an ovenproof dish with 1 tbsp of the oil, the garlic and oregano. Roast for 10 minutes.
Nestle the cod fillets in, drizzle with the rest of the oil and season.
Bake for 15-18 minutes, until the fish flakes easily. Scatter the olives over the grown-ups' side for the last 5 minutes.
Put the couscous in a bowl, pour over the hot stock, cover and leave for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Stir a squeeze of lemon and the parsley through the couscous.
Serve the cod, tomatoes and chickpeas on the couscous.
recipe.tip: Mathilda: keep her portion olive-free and check carefully for bones.
